strings.text: Agentic S4's output contract, and the reducer from outcomes to findings and verdicts.
Parse a batched reply, tolerating a bare single outcome from a one-unit batch.
Fan one batched reply out to per-unit replies that `reduce_outcomes` reads unchanged.
Parse one session's raw reply into an `InvestigationOutcome`, or `None`, never raising.
*f*'s normalised CWE, falling back to the unit's when the model omitted a usable one.
One reported finding anchored at *line_start*, carrying *f*'s prose verbatim.
*f*'s `also_cwes`, normalised and deduped, minus any `same_weakness` match for *primary*, capped at *max_extra*.
Fan *f* out over its repeat sites and its surviving co-located weakness classes, with `file` resolved to inventory form.
Reduce every session's raw reply into findings plus a per-unit verdict map, where a lost session reads as failed or uninvestigated rather than clean.
Fold anything not int-like to 0 so one malformed integer cannot fail the whole outcome and discard the unit's findings.
sink_line
line_end
Fold each malformed repeat site to 0, which `fan_out` skips, costing that site and not the finding.
repeat_lines
uninvestigated
Exactly one most-specific CWE id, e.g. CWE-89.
Repo-relative path, from this threat's FILES list.
1-indexed FIRST line of the weakness's span. For a handler or block the span may start at its decorator or signature — `sink_line`, not this field, names the dangerous statement itself.
Exact 1-indexed line of the single statement that embodies the defect — the dangerous call, query, render, write or cookie-set. 0 when no single statement does (e.g. a missing control).

1-indexed LAST line of the weakness, inclusive — the end of the vulnerable statement, block or handler, NOT a repeat of line_start. Span the whole construct: an unguarded route runs from its decorator to the end of its function body. Use 0 only when you genuinely cannot bound it.

Other DISTINCT weakness classes present at this same location, as CWE ids. One location routinely holds several: a cookie set without HttpOnly (CWE-1004) is usually also set without Secure (CWE-614); a route with no CSRF token (CWE-352) often also has no authorization check (CWE-862). Each id here becomes its own reported finding at this line, so naming one costs a few characters and omitting it loses a real defect. Do not list a parent or sibling of `cwe` that means the same thing — only genuinely different weaknesses.

When this IDENTICAL defect repeats at other call sites in the SAME file, the first line of every additional site — one integer each, no prose. The description you already wrote is reused verbatim for each, so listing a site costs you almost nothing while omitting it loses the finding entirely. Report the sites, never a summary of them: one finding whose line span swallows several call sites is wrong, and so is picking one site and dropping the rest. Leave empty only when the defect genuinely occurs once.

What must independently be true, beyond reaching this code, for the weakness to be exploitable — one concrete condition per entry, not a restatement of `description`. Name the actual gate: the endpoint is reachable by an unauthenticated caller; a feature flag or config value is set a particular way; the attacker needs a specific input shape (a negative amount, an oversized payload, a crafted redirect target); the caller needs a particular role or an active session. A reviewer judging exploitability off your report alone needs these named, so listing one costs a few words while omitting it loses real context. Leave empty only when the weakness fires unconditionally on any input that reaches this code — never as a default for not having checked.
before
before
Weakness class; unrecognized labels fold to OTHER.
One line, at most 12 words, naming the weakness and its location. No prose.
One enum value. s6 re-scores every finding from a CVSS vector, so do not argue it here.

AT MOST TWO SENTENCES: the defect and why it is one. The code is quoted for the reader already — do not restate it, do not repeat the title, and do not re-derive the exploit (exploit_scenario covers that) or the fix (recommendation covers that).

Concrete input -> impact, in at most five sentences. Every application feature, flow or component the scenario relies on or leads to (a password-reset flow, an admin panel, mail sending, a file store) must be one you saw in this repository's code; where the follow-on depends on one you did not see, write it conditionally ('if the application offers a password reset') or stop at the impact the code shows. A consequence the code does not support is a false claim, not a stronger finding.
AT MOST TWO SENTENCES: the concrete change, naming the API or control to use. No restatement of the defect, no alternatives list, no code block.
Echo the UNIT id you were given, verbatim.
confirmed
refuted
inconclusive
refuted = you read the whole surface and the claim does not hold; say why in rationale. inconclusive = you could not reach the evidence. Do NOT use confirmed as a default.
Why, in 1-3 sentences. Required for refuted.
EVERY distinct weakness class you have evidence for — a list, not one. Empty is correct and expected when verdict is refuted.
ONE entry per UNIT you were given, each echoing that unit's own id. Report every unit, including the ones you refuted — a unit you omit is recorded as uninvestigated, not clean.
